messages:
From: Claire Bell <claire.bell@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Data erase certification for private VPC: next steps

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the helpful overview in our vendor intake call. As we prepare to decommission our tenant in Redwood’s private VPC, our compliance team needs a clear path and evidence for a full customer-controlled erase. Specifically they asked for:

- A step-by-step plan for destroying customer data (including snapshots, backups, object storage, and any replicated copies).
- Confirmation on whether any customer data remains encrypted under customer-managed keys (CMK) or Redwood-managed keys, and the process for key revocation/zeroization.
- An expected timeline from kickoff to completion (including a canary/verification step).
- The artifacts you can provide after the run (delete logs, snapshot ids/hashes, KMS event ids, signed certificate).

We are operating under a hard compliance window and would like to target completion by 2026-11-30. Can you outline what you need from us (preferred cutoff time, export of data before wipe, POA for access) and what Redwood will deliver?

Appreciate a concise plan and whether you can produce a signed delete certificate for Clearwater Health.

Best,
Claire Bell
Dir, Compliance
Clearwater Health

Attachments: none
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Claire Bell <claire.bell@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data erase certification for private VPC: next steps

Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. High level: we can support a customer-controlled erase in a private deployment with a chain-of-custody and a signed certificate. Below is a proposed phased plan (we’ll refine after Dev and CS confirm):

1) Pre-kickoff (you): confirm final cutoff date and whether you need a data export. Provide an authorized POA contact for the run.
2) Runbook prep (Redwood): coordinate a blackout window, create a destruction ticket (HS-7894), stage delete artifacts template, and schedule infra job.
3) Execution (Redwood infra): snapshot tombstone + cross-region snapshot purge, object-store lifecycle purge, revoke CMKs or rotate and zeroize keys as requested, delete replication metadata, scrub ephemeral caches.
4) Verification (joint): run a canary verification (small set of records) and generate proof-of-delete report with hashes and KMS event ids.
5) Certification: deliver signed delete-certificate (PDF) and attach the proof-of-delete report. Optionally provide third-party attestation.

I’ve attached an outline we typically use (redwood-erase-process-outline.pdf). @dev_patel and @marissa_cole — can you confirm the technical steps below and whether 11/30 is feasible if we kick off next week? Also note: we may need a short scheduled window (~2–4 hours) to run the destructive job; I’ll coordinate exact timing once infra confirms.

Markus Klein
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data erase certification for private VPC: next steps

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 12:30 PM markus_klein@redwood.com wrote:
> I’ve attached an outline we typically use (redwood-erase-process-outline.pdf). @dev_patel and @marissa_cole — can you confirm the technical steps below and whether 11/30 is feasible if we kick off next week?

Summary of technical process and caveats:

- Scope: We will target all customer-owned objects in the mounted tenant bucket(s), all snapshot images created by Redwood for that tenant, KV cache shards, and any ephemeral local SSD contents for the dedicated nodes assigned to the tenant.
- Snapshots: We will locate all snapshot IDs and delete them across regions. Where snapshots were replicated we will remove replication metadata and scrub destination copies.
- Object storage: Run lifecycle deletion and then a final pass removing object versions and delete markers. Note: object-level delete is eventual; we run a multi-pass to ensure no versioned objects remain.
- Backups: If Clearwater was asked to retain third-party backups (e.g., exported DB dumps stored externally), Redwood cannot remove those; please confirm if you want us to proceed with Redwood-hosted copies only.
- Keys: If using CMKs (customer-managed), we will coordinate with your KMS admin to revoke/disable keys or, if you prefer, we can rotate keys and then run zeroization on ephemeral hardware. For Redwood-managed keys, we will perform key material zeroization and provide KMS event ids.
- Chain-of-custody logs: We will produce a run log (job id + timestamps), list of deleted object ids, snapshot ids, and KMS events. We can include SHA256 hashes for a sample set if you want cryptographic proof.
- Timing: With a scheduled window and all authorizations, 11/30 is achievable — we recommend booking a slot on 2026-11-29 UTC window to avoid region busy hours. Final completion (artifact delivery) can happen within 48 hours afterward.

I’m attaching the internal wipe runbook fragment we will execute (wipe-runbook.md). We’ll need a confirmed POA and a signed DPA amendment (if Clearwater requires legal language around deletion).

Dev Patel
Sr. Infra Engineer, Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference

Attachments: wipe-runbook.md
